title: Two heirs in a year
hook: his son Kharak Singh sickened and died, and his grandson Nau Nihal Singh was killed by a falling arch

segments.voice: Yesterday, his death, and your line was even kings fell short. Where did you see someone fall short, and keep what was good? Today, the kingdom without its founder. Day nine hundred twenty-six.

A young prince walks back from his father's cremation, through a gateway in Lahore. He's strong, clever, already a commander, the heir the court was watching. Mourners walk with him, the smoke of the pyre still in their clothes. Overhead, stones shift. The archway comes down, and the prince is struck. The kingdom that looked so solid has cremated one king that morning, and now its heir is down among the fallen stones. Today: two heirs in a year.
screen: `BACK FROM A FATHER'S CREMATION.` → `A GATEWAY IN LAHORE.` → `THE ARCH COMES DOWN.`

segments.voice: First, the son. Kharak Singh, the Maharaja's eldest, took the throne. Histories describe him as gentle and not suited to the hard politics of the court. Power slipped quickly into other hands, among them his own son's and the ministers'. His favorite adviser was killed, and later Kharak Singh himself fell ill and died. Some at the time suspected poison. Nobody can say for certain. Second, the grandson. Nau Nihal Singh, Kharak Singh's son, was young, able and ambitious, and he had already been ruling in all but name. On the day of his father's cremation, as he passed under a gateway, part of it fell and struck him. He died of his injuries. Third, the doubt. Histories record the suspicion that it was no accident. Some point to the ministers who gained from his death, and say the story of what happened in the hours after was kept close. Others say the arch simply fell. The sources don't settle it, and we won't pretend they do. Fourth, what it shows. The Maharaja had spent a lifetime building a kingdom. Within a short time of his death, his son and grandson were both gone, and the throne was open to whoever could seize it. A kingdom can look like a fortress and still hang by a thread, or by the stones of one gateway.
screen: `KHARAK SINGH TAKES THE THRONE AND FALLS ILL.` · `NAU NIHAL SINGH AND THE FALLING ARCH.` · `AN ACCIDENT, OR NOT?` · `A KINGDOM HANGING BY A THREAD.` · then, large: `POWER IS FRAGILE.`

segments.voice: Two minutes with fragile power. Sit, and let your breath settle. Think of one kind of power you hold: a title, a role in your family, money, health, influence over someone. Picture how it could be gone tomorrow, not with fear, just honestly. Then ask: if it went, what would still be there? Rest in that, breath by breath. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Kharak Singh, who sickened and died; his son Nau Nihal Singh was struck by a falling arch on the day of his father's cremation, two heirs lost in a year. Today's word.
Your line: power is fragile. Today, use whatever power you have gently, as if you'll only hold it for a little while. Day nine hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Sikhs meet the deaths of Kharak Singh and Nau Nihal Singh in histories of the years after Maharaja Ranjit Singh, when the Lahore throne passed quickly from hand to hand.

notes: Index title says 'in a year'; the voice says 'in a matter of months' and 'within a short time' to avoid a number; confirm.
Kharak Singh's favorite adviser (Chet Singh Bajwa) killed; suspicion of poisoning: confirm framing.
Hook calls him the heir the court was watching; confirm.
Suspicion of the Dogra ministers (Dhian Singh) over the arch is only hinted at ('ministers who gained'); confirm fairness.
Original-language word left null (no single Gurmukhi term for this day).

Editor: hook's 'by the end of that day ... lost its second ruler in a matter of months' was an ambiguous count and timing claim (the hook's death timing is not in the voice's source); replaced with 'has buried one king, and now its heir is down among the fallen stones'; teach ending changed from the repeated 'That's today's line' to end on the gateway.

Auditor: hook said the kingdom had 'buried' a king, but Kharak Singh was cremated (the hook itself says so); changed to 'cremated'. 'died not long after' the adviser's killing understated about a year (Chet Singh killed 1839, Kharak Singh died November 1840); now 'later'.
